title: 路上與行程安排
subtitle: Getting around town and planning what to do

example.hanzi: 我想買一輛新的腳踏車。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí liàng xīn de jiǎotàchē.
example.gloss: I want to buy a new bicycle.

example.hanzi: 我家離捷運站只有兩百米。
example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí jiéyùn zhàn zhǐyǒu liǎngbǎi mǐ.
example.gloss: My home is only two hundred meters from the MRT station.

example.hanzi: 這段路有點遠，走過去要十分鐘。
example.pinyin: Zhè duàn lù yǒudiǎn yuǎn, zǒu guòqù yào shí fēnzhōng.
example.gloss: This stretch of road is a bit far; it takes ten minutes to walk.

vocab.gloss: to pass; to go through; process

example.hanzi: 我每天上班都會經過那家咖啡店。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shàngbān dōu huì jīngguò nà jiā kāfēi diàn.
example.gloss: I pass by that coffee shop every day on my way to work.

vocab.gloss: at last; in the end; finally

example.hanzi: 等了很久，公車終於來了。
example.pinyin: Děng le hěn jiǔ, gōngchē zhōngyú lái le.
example.gloss: After waiting a long time, the bus finally came.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zài Táiwān zhù le duō jiǔ le?
example.gloss: How long have you lived in Taiwan?

grammar.title: 用「終於」說「總算等到了」
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 終於 + 動詞 + 了
grammar.explanation: 「終於」放在動詞前面，表示等了很久、花了很多力氣以後，想要的事情發生了。句尾常常加「了」，前面常先說明等待的過程，像「等了很久」「走了一段路」「經過三個站」。它帶有鬆一口氣、開心的感覺，所以後面接的多半是好事。
grammar.contrast: 「終於」和「最後」很容易搞錯。「最後」只是說順序上的最後一件事，沒有感情：「我先吃飯，最後喝茶。」「終於」一定要有「等很久／很難」的意思：「我等了一個鐘頭，終於吃到了。」如果只是講順序，用「最後」；如果想說「總算」，用「終於」。
grammar.common_error: Learners copy English word order and put it at the end of the sentence ('The bus came finally') — 公車來了終於 is wrong; 終於 must come before the verb. They also use it for plain sequencing ('first... then... finally'), where Chinese needs 最後.

examples.hanzi: 等了很久，那輛公車終於來了。
examples.pinyin: Děng le hěn jiǔ, nà liàng gōngchē zhōngyú lái le.
examples.gloss: After a long wait, that bus finally came.

examples.hanzi: 走了一段路，我們終於到了夜市。
examples.pinyin: Zǒu le yí duàn lù, wǒmen zhōngyú dào le yèshì.
examples.gloss: After walking a stretch of road, we finally got to the night market.

examples.hanzi: 經過兩家便利商店，我終於找到那家店了。
examples.pinyin: Jīngguò liǎng jiā biànlì shāngdiàn, wǒ zhōngyú zhǎodào nà jiā diàn le.
examples.gloss: After passing two convenience stores, I finally found that shop.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 請問，捷運站離這裡遠不遠？
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, jiéyùn zhàn lí zhèlǐ yuǎn bù yuǎn?
dialogue.gloss: Excuse me, is the MRT station far from here?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 不遠喔，只有三百米左右。
dialogue.pinyin: Bù yuǎn ō, zhǐyǒu sānbǎi mǐ zuǒyòu.
dialogue.gloss: Not far — only about three hundred meters.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 太好了，我等公車等很久了，還是走路吧。
dialogue.pinyin: Tài hǎo le, wǒ děng gōngchē děng hěn jiǔ le, háishì zǒulù ba.
dialogue.gloss: Great. I've been waiting for the bus a long time; I'll just walk.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 你直走，經過那家便利商店，再左轉就到了。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ zhí zǒu, jīngguò nà jiā biànlì shāngdiàn, zài zuǒ zhuǎn jiù dào le.
dialogue.gloss: Go straight, pass that convenience store, then turn left and you're there.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.hanzi: 耶，我看到一輛公車開過去了，早知道就搭車。
dialogue.pinyin: Yé, wǒ kàndào yí liàng gōngchē kāi guòqù le, zǎo zhīdào jiù dā chē.
dialogue.gloss: Hey, I just saw a bus drive by — I should have taken it.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.hanzi: 這段路很快啦，五分鐘就走到了！
dialogue.pinyin: Zhè duàn lù hěn kuài la, wǔ fēnzhōng jiù zǒudào le!
dialogue.gloss: This stretch is quick — you'll walk it in five minutes!

sentences.gloss: This stretch of road is very long.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ jiā lí xuéxiào zhǐyǒu sānbǎi mǐ.
sentences.gloss: My home is only three hundred meters from school.
The bus passes the post office.

sentences.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú mǎi le yí liàng jīchē.

passage.title: 騎車去夜市
passage.hanzi: 上個週末，我跟朋友騎腳踏車去夜市。那段路有點遠，也下了一點雨。我們經過一家便利商店，進去買了兩瓶水。休息了一下，又騎了三千米，終於到了。夜市裡的人真多，我們吃了臭豆腐和牛肉麵，也喝了珍珠奶茶。回家的時候太累了，我們搭了一輛計程車。
passage.gloss: Last weekend my friend and I rode our bikes to the night market. That stretch of road was a bit far, and it rained a little. We passed a convenience store and went in to buy two bottles of water. After resting a while, we rode another three thousand meters and finally arrived. There were so many people at the night market; we ate stinky tofu and beef noodles, and drank bubble tea too. On the way home we were too tired, so we took a taxi.

vocab.gloss: to plan; to intend; to calculate

example.hanzi: 我週末打算去台北看朋友。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò dǎsuàn qù Táiběi kàn péngyǒu.
example.gloss: I plan to go to Taipei to see friends this weekend.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yòu wàngjì dài Yōuyóukǎ le.
example.gloss: I forgot to bring my EasyCard again.

example.hanzi: 剛才我在樓下遇到老師。
example.pinyin: Gāngcái wǒ zài lóuxià yùdào lǎoshī.
example.gloss: Just now I ran into the teacher downstairs.

vocab.gloss: to dare; daring; (polite) may I venture

example.gloss: I don't dare eat stinky tofu.

example.pinyin: Nǐ yuànyì bāng wǒ yíge máng ma?
example.gloss: Are you willing to do me a favour?

vocab.gloss: to agree; to consent; to approve

example.hanzi: 我媽不同意我買新的腳踏車。
example.pinyin: Wǒ mā bù tóngyì wǒ mǎi xīn de jiǎotàchē.
example.gloss: My mum doesn't agree to me buying a new bike.

grammar.title: 打算 + Verb Phrase: stating a plan
grammar.explanation: 打算 is a verb meaning 'to plan to'. It goes right after the subject and is followed by another verb phrase, never by a noun alone. To say you don't plan to do something, put 不 in front: 不打算. Because 打算 talks about something not yet done, it does not take 了 or 過, and you can ask about someone's plan with 打算怎麼…? or 打算做什麼?
grammar.contrast: 想 vs 要 vs 打算: 想 is 'feel like / would like' (just a wish), 要 is 'want to / be going to' (a decision, often with a time or condition), and 打算 means you have actually worked the plan out in your head. 我想去台北 = I'd like to go; 我打算去台北 = I'm planning on it.
grammar.common_error: Learners treat 打算 like an adjective or add 了: 我很打算去 or 我打算了去. 打算 is a verb, so no 很, and no 了 after it — just say 我打算去.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ míngnián dǎsuàn qù Rìběn wán.
examples.gloss: I plan to travel to Japan next year.
How do you plan to get to the airport?
He doesn't plan to change jobs.

grammar.title: 願意 / 敢 / 同意 before a verb
grammar.pattern: Subject + 願意 / 敢 / 同意 + Verb Phrase
grammar.explanation: These three verbs all take another verb after them. 願意 = be willing to; 敢 = dare to; 同意 = agree to (someone doing something). Negate them all with 不: 不願意、不敢、不同意。
grammar.contrast: 願意 vs 敢: 願意 is about willingness (you could, but do you want to?), 敢 is about courage (are you afraid?). 我不願意去 means I don't want to; 我不敢去 means I'm scared to.
grammar.common_error: Saying 我很敢 or 我沒敢 — use 不敢 for the negative, and don't use 很 with 敢 in everyday speech.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn yuànyì jiāo wǒmen chànggē.
examples.gloss: She's very willing to teach us to sing.

examples.hanzi: 我不敢一個人走那條路。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù gǎn yíge rén zǒu nà tiáo lù.
examples.gloss: I don't dare walk down that road alone.

examples.hanzi: 老闆同意我今天早一點回家。
examples.pinyin: Lǎobǎn tóngyì wǒ jīntiān zǎo yìdiǎn huí jiā.
examples.gloss: The boss agreed to let me go home a bit earlier today.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 剛才我打電話給你，你怎麼沒接？
dialogue.pinyin: Gāngcái wǒ dǎ diànhuà gěi nǐ, nǐ zěnme méi jiē?
dialogue.gloss: I called you a moment ago — how come you didn't pick up?

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.hanzi: 對不起，我忘記把手機帶出來了。
dialogue.pinyin: Duìbùqǐ, wǒ wàngjì bǎ shǒujī dài chūlái le.
dialogue.gloss: Sorry, I forgot to bring my phone out with me.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 沒關係。你這個週末打算做什麼？
dialogue.pinyin: Méi guānxi. Nǐ zhège zhōumò dǎsuàn zuò shénme?
dialogue.gloss: Never mind. What are you planning to do this weekend?

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.hanzi: 我想去看電影，你願意跟我一起去嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù kàn diànyǐng, nǐ yuànyì gēn wǒ yìqǐ qù ma?
dialogue.gloss: I want to see a movie — would you be willing to come with me?

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 好啊，不過我不敢太晚回家，我爸不同意。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo a, búguò wǒ bù gǎn tài wǎn huí jiā, wǒ bà bù tóngyì.
dialogue.gloss: Sure, but I don't dare get home too late — my dad doesn't allow it.

dialogue.speaker: 小文
dialogue.hanzi: 那我們看早一點的，六點就搭捷運回來。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒmen kàn zǎo yìdiǎn de, liù diǎn jiù dā jiéyùn huílái.
dialogue.gloss: Then let's see an earlier one and take the MRT back at six.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ gāngcái wàngjì gēn nǐ shuō.
sentences.gloss: I forgot to tell you just now.
How do you plan to get home?

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ bù gǎn yíge rén zuò fēijī.
sentences.gloss: I don't dare take a plane by myself.
He's willing to teach me Chinese.

sentences.pinyin: Bàba tóngyì wǒ mǎi nà shuāng xié.
sentences.gloss: Dad agreed to let me buy that pair of shoes.

passage.title: 我的週末打算
passage.hanzi: 剛才哥哥問我週末打算做什麼。我說我想一個人坐火車去台北，先去看朋友，晚上再去吃牛肉麵。哥哥不太同意，他說我常常忘記帶悠遊卡和錢，也不敢跟別人問路。最後他願意跟我一起去，我覺得這樣也不錯。
passage.gloss: Just now my older brother asked me what I was planning to do this weekend. I said I wanted to take the train to Taipei by myself — first visit a friend, then go eat beef noodles in the evening. My brother wasn't too happy about it; he said I often forget to bring my EasyCard and money, and I don't dare ask strangers for directions. In the end he was willing to go with me, and I think that's not bad either.
